questions.q: When does an AFTER trigger run?
options: Before the triggering statement runs, to validate it in advance
In a completely separate transaction, after the original one has already committed
After the triggering INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE completes, inside the same transaction, before it commits
Only once per day, on a schedule
questions.explain: AFTER triggers fire after the data change happens but still inside the same transaction, so the trigger can still affect whether that transaction commits.

questions.q: On an UPDATE, which pseudo-table(s) are populated inside the trigger?
options: Both inserted (new values) and deleted (old values)
Only deleted
Only inserted
Neither — UPDATE triggers get the data from the base table directly
questions.explain: An UPDATE populates deleted with the row's before-values and inserted with its after-values, which is how a single trigger can capture both an old and a new value.

questions.q: What happens if an AFTER trigger's body issues ROLLBACK TRANSACTION?
options: Nothing — ROLLBACK is not allowed inside a trigger
The trigger is permanently disabled for future statements
The entire original triggering operation is undone, not just the trigger's own work
Only the trigger's INSERT into its own audit table is undone
questions.explain: Because the trigger runs inside the same transaction as the triggering statement, a ROLLBACK there undoes the whole operation, including the row changes that appeared to have already happened.

questions.q: On a plain DELETE, which pseudo-table holds the removed rows?
options: removed
old
deleted
inserted
questions.explain: deleted always holds the "before" picture — the rows as they were before the DELETE (or UPDATE) removed or changed them.

questions.q: Can a single AFTER trigger be defined to fire on more than one kind of statement?
options: No — a separate trigger is required for each of INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE
Only if the table has no primary key
Yes — AFTER INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE fires the same trigger body for any of the three
Only INSERT and UPDATE can share a trigger, never DELETE
questions.explain: CREATE TRIGGER ... AFTER INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE AS ... lets one trigger body run for any of those three events; the body can check which one happened if it needs to branch.
